creators.name: Antony Gormley
creators.bio: British sculptor who casts his own body in iron and steel and places the figures on beaches, rooftops, mountains and salt lakes, from Another Place to the Angel of the North.
creators.why: He shows that a single human figure placed in a landscape turns the whole place into a stage and changes how every passer-by reads it.
creators.bio_zh: 英国雕塑家，用自己的身体翻模铸成铁或钢的人像，把它们安放在海滩、屋顶、山坡和盐湖上，代表作有《Another Place》和《Angel of the North》。
creators.why_zh: 他证明了：把一个人形放进风景里，整个地方就变成了舞台，每个路人对它的理解都会随之改变。

creators.name: Xavi Bou
creators.bio: Barcelona photographer trained in geology who, since 2012, stacks video frames of birds in flight into single images (Ornithographies) that reveal the shapes their paths draw in the sky.
creators.why: His digital chronophotography is the clearest model for AR trails: it makes an invisible path in the real sky visible without changing the sky.
creators.bio_zh: 出身地质学的巴塞罗那摄影师，自 2012 年起把飞鸟视频的连续帧叠合成一张图像（Ornithographies），让鸟在天空中画出的轨迹显形。
creators.why_zh: 他的数字连续摄影是 AR 轨迹效果最清楚的范本：不改变天空，只让真实天空中看不见的路径显形。

creators.name: Andy Goldsworthy
creators.bio: British artist who works with leaves, ice, stone, wood and the tide, making both ephemeral pieces that melt or wash away and permanent walls and cairns.
creators.why: His work teaches that time, weather and decay can be part of a piece, which is exactly what a persistent, site-anchored AR work has to design for.
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，用树叶、冰、石头、木头和潮水创作，既有会融化、被冲走的短暂作品，也有长期存在的石墙和石堆。
creators.why_zh: 他的作品说明时间、天气和衰败都可以成为作品的一部分，这正是长期锚定在某地的 AR 作品需要设计的东西。

creators.name: Christo and Jeanne-Claude
creators.bio: Artist couple who wrapped buildings and coastlines in fabric and ran fences, curtains, gates and floating piers across landscapes for two or three weeks at a time, financing every project themselves.
creators.why: They proved that a temporary layer laid over a familiar place makes people see its true shape, the core promise of AR overlays.
creators.bio_zh: 艺术家夫妇，用织物包裹建筑和海岸，在风景中架设围栏、帘幕、门廊和浮桥，每件作品只存在两三周，全部自筹资金完成。
creators.why_zh: 他们证明了：在熟悉的地方覆盖一层临时的表层，反而让人看清它原本的形状，这正是 AR 叠加的核心承诺。

creators.name: Robert Smithson
creators.bio: American artist (1938–1973) and founding figure of Land Art, best known for Spiral Jetty, a 457-metre coil of basalt in Utah's Great Salt Lake.
creators.why: He made scale, entropy and the view from the air part of the artwork, a vocabulary AR designers reuse for world-scale content.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家（1938–1973），大地艺术的奠基人之一，代表作是犹他州大盐湖中长 457 米的玄武岩螺旋《Spiral Jetty》。
creators.why_zh: 他把尺度、熵和空中视角纳入作品，这套语汇正是 AR 设计世界尺度内容时要借用的。

creators.name: Nancy Holt
creators.bio: American artist (1938–2014) whose concrete tunnels, rings and pipes frame the sun, stars and horizon at precise moments such as the solstices.
creators.why: Her works are physical viewfinders aligned to the sky, the same logic as an AR anchor that only resolves from one place at one time.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家（1938–2014），她用混凝土隧道、圆环和管道在特定时刻（如至日）精确框住太阳、星星和地平线。
creators.why_zh: 她的作品是对准天空的实体取景器，与只在某个地点、某个时刻才成立的 AR 锚点逻辑相同。
creators.based_zh: 纽约 / 新墨西哥，美国

creators.name: Walter De Maria
creators.bio: American artist (1935–2013) known for The Lightning Field, 400 steel poles on a grid in the New Mexico desert, and for rooms filled with earth.
creators.why: He turned a measured grid into a device for watching light, weather and time, a lesson in how few elements an augmented landscape needs.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家（1935–2013），以新墨西哥沙漠中 400 根不锈钢杆组成的网格《The Lightning Field》和装满泥土的房间闻名。
creators.why_zh: 他把精确测量的网格变成观看光、天气和时间的装置，说明增强一片风景只需要极少的元素。

creators.name: Richard Long
creators.bio: British artist who since 1967 has made art by walking: lines trodden into grass, stone circles and text works that record routes across the world.
creators.why: A Line Made by Walking is the first 'trace' artwork: the body's path becomes the drawing, exactly what location-based AR records.
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，自 1967 年起以行走为创作：在草地上踩出线条，摆放石圈，并用文字记录他走过的世界各地路线。
creators.why_zh: 《A Line Made by Walking》是最早的“痕迹”作品之一：身体的路径就是绘画，这正是基于位置的 AR 所记录的东西。

creators.name: Michael Heizer
creators.bio: American artist who cuts and moves the desert at monumental scale: Double Negative, Levitated Mass and City, a mile-long complex he built in Nevada over five decades.
creators.why: His negative spaces and suspended boulder show how absence and implied danger can be designed, useful for AR that subtracts rather than adds.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，以巨大尺度切割和搬运沙漠：《Double Negative》《Levitated Mass》，以及他在内华达用五十年建成、长约一英里的《City》。
creators.why_zh: 他的“负空间”和悬空巨石展示了如何设计缺失和隐含的危险感，对做减法而非加法的 AR 很有启发。

creators.name: Charles Ross
creators.role: Artist working with light and astronomy
creators.bio: American artist known for prisms and solar burns and for Star Axis, a naked-eye observatory carved into a New Mexico mesa and aligned with Earth's axis.
creators.why: Star Axis makes a 26,000-year cycle walkable, a model for AR that ties a physical path to astronomical data.
creators.role_zh: 以光与天文为材料的艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，以棱镜和“太阳灼烧”作品闻名，代表作《Star Axis》是开凿在新墨西哥台地中、对准地轴的肉眼天文台。
creators.why_zh: 《Star Axis》让一个 26000 年的周期变得可以用脚走完，是把实体路径和天文数据绑定的 AR 范本。
creators.based_zh: 纽约 / 新墨西哥，美国

creators.name: Maya Lin
creators.bio: American artist and architect who designed the Vietnam Veterans Memorial as a student and makes earthworks and environmental memorials such as Wavefield and Ghost Forest.
creators.why: She shapes land and names so that information (lost lives, lost species) is felt by walking, an approach AR memorials can borrow.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家、建筑师，学生时代设计了越战纪念碑，之后创作了《Wavefield》《Ghost Forest》等大地作品与环境纪念作品。
creators.why_zh: 她塑造土地和名字，让信息（逝去的生命、消失的物种）通过行走被感受到，这种方式值得 AR 纪念作品借鉴。

creators.name: Agnes Denes
creators.bio: Hungarian-born American pioneer of ecological art who planted two acres of wheat on a Manhattan landfill in 1982 and a mountain of 11,000 trees in Finland.
creators.why: Her works put a living system into the wrong place to make a value system visible, a strong template for AR critique.
creators.role_zh: 观念艺术家、环境艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 出生于匈牙利的美国生态艺术先驱，1982 年在曼哈顿垃圾填埋地种下两英亩小麦，又在芬兰种出由 11000 棵树组成的山。
creators.why_zh: 她把一个活的系统放在“不该出现”的地方，让一套价值观显形，这是 AR 批判性作品的有力模板。

creators.name: Chris Drury
creators.bio: British artist who builds stone and turf 'cloud chambers', camera obscuras that project the sky onto the floor, and earthworks based on patterns of weather, water and the body.
creators.why: His cloud chambers are pre-digital passthrough: a dark room that shows the outside world live, the ancestor of the AR viewport.
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，用石头和草皮建造“云室”（把天空投到地面上的暗箱），并以天气、水和人体的纹样创作大地作品。
creators.why_zh: 他的云室是前数字时代的“透视”：一间暗室实时呈现外面的世界，是 AR 取景窗的祖先。

creators.name: Doug Aitken
creators.bio: American artist whose mirrored house (Mirage), mirrored hot-air balloon (New Horizon) and underwater pavilions dissolve architecture into the landscape it reflects.
creators.why: Mirrored volumes act like real-world shaders: the object is only the landscape, reframed, which is a clean idea for AR materials.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，他的镜面房屋《Mirage》、镜面热气球《New Horizon》和水下展亭让建筑消融在它所映照的风景里。
creators.why_zh: 镜面体块就像现实世界里的着色器：物体本身只是被重新框取的风景，这是 AR 材质设计的简洁思路。

creators.name: Tomás Saraceno
creators.bio: Argentine artist who builds cloud-like modules, walkable nets and Aerocene, a community of solar-powered balloons that fly without fossil fuels.
creators.why: He treats air, spiders' webs and the sky as shared media, a useful frame for multi-user AR that lives in the air above us.
creators.bio_zh: 阿根廷艺术家，创作云状模块、可行走的网，以及 Aerocene：一个不用化石燃料、仅靠太阳加热升空的气球社群项目。
creators.why_zh: 他把空气、蛛网和天空当作共享媒介，这对漂浮在头顶的多人 AR 很有参考价值。

creators.name: Jaume Plensa
creators.bio: Spanish sculptor of monumental heads made of letters, mesh or white stone, placed in plazas, parks and on the waterfront, including Chicago's Crown Fountain.
creators.why: His giant, eyes-closed faces show how a single calm figure can change the mood of a whole public space, a lesson for AR avatars in cities.
creators.bio_zh: 西班牙雕塑家，以字母、网格或白色石材塑造巨大头像，安放在广场、公园和水岸，包括芝加哥的《Crown Fountain》。
creators.why_zh: 他那些闭着眼睛的巨大面孔说明，一个安静的形象就能改变整个公共空间的气氛，这是城市 AR 形象的一课。

creators.name: Anish Kapoor
creators.bio: British-Indian sculptor of mirror-polished and void-like forms such as Cloud Gate in Chicago, Sky Mirror and the whirlpool Descension.
creators.why: His reflective public works turn the sky and the crowd into the content of the sculpture, the same trick as environment-mapped AR objects.
creators.bio_zh: 英籍印度裔雕塑家，以镜面抛光和“虚空”形态著称，如芝加哥的《Cloud Gate》《Sky Mirror》和漩涡作品《Descension》。
creators.why_zh: 他的镜面公共作品把天空和人群变成雕塑的内容，与使用环境贴图的 AR 物体是同一个把戏。

creators.name: Rob Mulholland
creators.bio: Scottish sculptor whose mirrored human figures stand in forests and lochs, reflecting their surroundings until they almost disappear.
creators.why: His mirror people are the physical version of an AR occlusion test: a figure that is present only through what it reflects.
creators.bio_zh: 苏格兰雕塑家，他的镜面人形站在森林和湖中，映照周围环境，几乎消失不见。
creators.why_zh: 他的镜面人像是 AR 遮挡测试的实体版本：一个只通过反射才显现的人形。

creators.name: Saype (Guillaume Legros)
creators.bio: French-Swiss artist who sprays giant figures onto grass with biodegradable paint made of chalk, charcoal and milk proteins; they fade as the grass grows.
creators.why: His paintings only resolve from the air or a distant slope, and they fade with time, two properties that location-based AR designers constantly deal with.
creators.bio_zh: 法国与瑞士艺术家，用粉笔、木炭和牛奶蛋白制成的可降解颜料在草地上喷绘巨大人像，草长高后画面便会消失。
creators.why_zh: 他的画只有从空中或远处的坡上才看得完整，而且会随时间消退，这两点正是位置型 AR 设计者经常要处理的。

creators.name: Jim Denevan
creators.bio: American artist who draws enormous geometric patterns with a stick or rake on beaches, deserts and frozen lakes, including a nine-square-mile drawing on Lake Baikal.
creators.why: His drawings are made at walking height but only read from the air, a direct lesson in designing for two viewpoints at once.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，用木棍或耙子在海滩、沙漠和冰冻湖面上画出巨大的几何图案，包括在贝加尔湖冰面上面积达九平方英里的作品。
creators.why_zh: 他的画在步行高度完成，却只能从空中读懂，直接说明了如何同时为两种视点设计。
creators.based_zh: 圣克鲁兹，加利福尼亚，美国

creators.name: Andres Amador
creators.bio: American artist who rakes vast geometric and organic patterns into beaches at low tide, knowing the sea will erase them within hours.
creators.why: His tide-bound drawings make impermanence a feature, and his group mandalas show how many people can co-draw one large image.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，在退潮的沙滩上耙出巨大的几何与有机图案，明知几小时后海水就会把它们抹去。
creators.why_zh: 他受潮汐限定的沙画把短暂变成了特色，他的集体曼陀罗也展示了多人如何共同画出一张巨图。

creators.name: Zadok Ben-David
creators.bio: Yemen-born, London-based sculptor known for fields of thousands of tiny etched-steel figures and flowers whose look changes completely as you walk around them.
creators.why: His two-sided fields show how the same objects can tell two stories depending on the viewer's position, a core AR idea.
creators.bio_zh: 出生于也门、定居伦敦的雕塑家，以成千上万个蚀刻钢片小人与小花组成的场域闻名，观者绕行时作品会完全变样。
creators.why_zh: 他的双面场域说明同一组物体会随观者位置讲出两个故事，这是 AR 的核心思路之一。

creators.name: Not Vital
creators.bio: Swiss artist who builds sculptural houses, towers and 'houses to watch the sunset' in remote places from Niger to Patagonia, and runs a sculpture park in the Engadin.
creators.why: His buildings exist mainly to frame one view or one moment of the day, a pure example of designing an experience around a place.
creators.bio_zh: 瑞士艺术家，在从尼日尔到巴塔哥尼亚的偏远地方建造雕塑般的房屋、塔楼和“看日落的房子”，并在恩加丁经营一座雕塑公园。
creators.why_zh: 他的建筑主要是为了框住某个景色或一天中的某个时刻，是围绕地点设计体验的纯粹例子。

creators.name: Pierre Huyghe
creators.bio: French artist who builds living, self-running environments with animals, bacteria, plants and algorithms, such as Untilled and After ALife Ahead.
creators.why: He designs systems rather than objects, so the work keeps changing whether or not anyone watches, a model for persistent AR worlds.
creators.bio_zh: 法国艺术家，用动物、细菌、植物和算法搭建能自行运转的活环境，如《Untilled》和《After ALife Ahead》。
creators.why_zh: 他设计的是系统而非物体，作品无论有没有人看都在变化，是持久型 AR 世界的范本。
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 圣地亚哥，智利

creators.name: Ai Weiwei (艾未未)
creators.bio: Chinese artist whose large public installations use everyday objects in huge numbers, from 100 million porcelain seeds to refugee life jackets wrapped around a concert hall.
creators.why: His works show how repeating one object thousands of times in a public place turns a statistic into something you can walk into.
creators.bio_zh: 中国艺术家，他的大型公共装置大量使用日常物件，从一亿颗瓷制葵花籽到包裹音乐厅的难民救生衣。
creators.why_zh: 他的作品说明，把一个物件在公共空间里重复成千上万次，就能把一个统计数字变成可以走进去的东西。

creators.name: Theo Jansen
creators.bio: Dutch artist who since 1990 has evolved Strandbeests, wind-powered walking creatures made of PVC tubes that roam the beaches of the Netherlands.
creators.why: Strandbeests make the wind visible as walking, and their generations show how iteration itself can be the artwork.
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰艺术家，自 1990 年起不断“进化”Strandbeest：用 PVC 管制成、靠风力行走、在荷兰海滩上游荡的“海滩生物”。
creators.why_zh: 海滩生物把风变成了可见的行走，而它们的一代代更迭说明迭代本身就可以是作品。

creators.name: Ugo Rondinone
creators.bio: Swiss artist who stacks huge boulders into colourful totems, most famously Seven Magic Mountains in the Nevada desert, and places stone giants in city plazas.
creators.why: His bright stacks against the desert show how colour and contrast alone make a virtual-feeling object in a real landscape.
creators.bio_zh: 瑞士艺术家，把巨石叠成色彩鲜艳的图腾，最著名的是内华达沙漠中的《Seven Magic Mountains》，也在城市广场上安放石头巨人。
creators.why_zh: 他在沙漠中的鲜艳石柱说明，只靠色彩和对比就能让真实风景中的物体产生“虚拟感”。

creators.name: Florentijn Hofman
creators.bio: Dutch artist of giant public sculptures of familiar toys and animals, above all the Rubber Duck that has floated in more than twenty harbours.
creators.why: His giant, cute objects in harbours are the physical version of the most viral AR move: take something small and familiar and make it huge in a real place.
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰艺术家，把熟悉的玩具和动物放大成巨型公共雕塑，最著名的是在二十多个港口漂浮过的《Rubber Duck》。
creators.why_zh: 他在港口放置的巨大可爱物体，正是最容易走红的 AR 手法的实体版：把熟悉的小东西放大到真实场景里。

creators.name: JR
creators.bio: French artist who pastes giant black-and-white photographs onto buildings, walls, rooftops and landscapes, and builds huge scaffolded figures and anamorphic collages.
creators.why: He shows how an image scaled to a place, and seen from the right point, can rewrite a building or a border, the core move of world-scale AR.
creators.bio_zh: 法国艺术家，把巨大的黑白照片贴在建筑、墙面、屋顶和风景上，也用脚手架搭建巨人形象和变形拼贴。
creators.why_zh: 他展示了：一张按场地放大、从正确位置观看的图像可以改写一栋建筑或一条边界，这是世界尺度 AR 的核心手法。
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 纽约，美国

creators.name: Jason deCaires Taylor
creators.bio: British sculptor who sinks cast human figures to the sea floor, where they become artificial reefs slowly overgrown by coral and algae.
creators.why: His underwater figures are an art work that nature keeps editing, a model for AR content that changes with its environment over time.
creators.bio_zh: 英国雕塑家，把人体翻模雕塑沉入海底，让它们成为人工礁石，慢慢被珊瑚和藻类覆盖。
creators.why_zh: 他的水下人像是一件由自然不断改写的作品，是随环境长期变化的 AR 内容的范本。

creators.name: Patrick Dougherty
creators.bio: American artist who weaves saplings and sticks into huge swirling huts and towers on museum lawns and campuses, built with local volunteers in about three weeks.
creators.why: His stickworks feel like drawings made in 3D space, an analogue reference for volumetric AR sketching.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，用树苗和枝条编织出巨大的漩涡状小屋和塔楼，通常与当地志愿者在约三周内建在博物馆草坪或校园上。
creators.why_zh: 他的枝条作品就像在三维空间里画出的线条，是体积化 AR 绘画的模拟参考。
creators.based_zh: 教堂山，北卡罗来纳，美国

creators.name: Thomas Dambo
creators.bio: Danish artist who builds giant trolls from scrap wood and hides them in forests around the world, each with a story and a treasure-map trail.
creators.why: His trolls are the physical version of location-based AR games: characters hidden in nature, found by following clues.
creators.bio_zh: 丹麦艺术家，用回收木料建造巨型巨魔，把它们藏在世界各地的森林里，每一个都有自己的故事和寻宝地图。
creators.why_zh: 他的巨魔是位置型 AR 游戏的实体版：藏在自然里的角色，跟着线索才找得到。

creators.name: Isaac Cordal
creators.bio: Spanish artist whose tiny cement figures of office workers and politicians (Cement Eclipses) are placed in gutters, on ledges and in puddles of cities worldwide.
creators.why: His miniatures show how scale and placement alone create a story in the street, a key idea for small AR figures on real surfaces.
creators.bio_zh: 西班牙艺术家，他的小型水泥人偶（上班族、政客，系列名《Cement Eclipses》）被放在世界各地城市的排水沟、窗台和水洼里。
creators.why_zh: 他的小人说明，只靠尺度和摆放位置就能在街头讲故事，对在真实表面放置小型 AR 角色很关键。

creators.name: Slinkachu
creators.bio: British artist behind Little People, a long-running project that leaves hand-painted model-railway figures in London streets and photographs them in tiny scenes.
creators.why: He proves that the smallest possible intervention, found by attentive passers-by, can be a complete artwork.
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，长期项目《Little People》把手绘的火车模型小人留在伦敦街头，拍成微型场景。
creators.why_zh: 他证明了最小的介入，只要被细心的路人发现，也可以是完整的作品。

creators.name: Bruno Catalano
creators.bio: French sculptor whose bronze travellers (Les Voyageurs) are missing large parts of their bodies, so the harbour or street behind them shows through.
creators.why: His fragmented figures are a physical diminished-reality effect: the missing part is filled by the real world.
creators.bio_zh: 法国雕塑家，他的青铜旅人系列《Les Voyageurs》身体缺失一大块，让背后的港口或街道透过来。
creators.why_zh: 他的残缺人像是一种实体的“削减现实”效果：缺失的部分由真实世界来填补。

creators.name: Mark Jenkins
creators.bio: American artist who casts life-size figures in packing tape, dresses them and places them in streets in odd poses, provoking passers-by.
creators.why: His hyper-real figures test how people react to a body where it should not be, the same social test AR characters face.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，用封箱胶带翻制等身人像，给它们穿上衣服，以奇怪的姿势放在街头，引起路人反应。
creators.why_zh: 他的逼真人像测试了人们如何反应于“不该出现的身体”，这也是 AR 角色要面对的社会测试。

creators.name: Lorenzo Quinn
creators.bio: Italian sculptor known for giant hands that rise out of Venice's canals to hold up buildings or join across water.
creators.why: His hands turn a whole city into the context of one gesture, a clear idea for scale and storytelling in city AR.
creators.bio_zh: 意大利雕塑家，以威尼斯运河中升起的巨手闻名，它们托住建筑或跨水相握。
creators.why_zh: 他的巨手让整座城市成为一个手势的背景，为城市 AR 的尺度与叙事提供了清晰思路。

creators.name: Alex Chinneck
creators.bio: British artist who makes buildings appear to melt, slide, float or unzip, using real bricks and engineering so the illusion holds in daylight.
creators.why: He does to real facades what AR filters promise to do, and shows how much the effect depends on exact, believable materials.
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，让建筑看起来在融化、滑落、漂浮或拉开拉链，用真实的砖和工程手段让错觉在白天也成立。
creators.why_zh: 他对真实立面所做的，正是 AR 滤镜承诺要做的事，也说明效果有多依赖精确可信的材质。

creators.name: Tatzu Nishi
creators.bio: Japanese artist who builds living rooms and hotel rooms around public monuments, so visitors meet a statue at eye level inside a domestic interior.
creators.why: He reframes a monument by changing the room around it, exactly what a portal or world-replacement AR effect does.
creators.bio_zh: 日本艺术家，围绕公共纪念碑搭建客厅或酒店房间，让观众在家居室内与雕像平视相遇。
creators.why_zh: 他通过改变纪念碑周围的房间来重新框定它，这正是 AR 传送门或“替换世界”效果所做的事。
creators.based_zh: 柏林，德国 / 东京，日本

creators.name: Kurt Perschke
creators.bio: American artist behind the RedBall Project, a 4.6-metre red inflatable ball squeezed into alleys, arches and doorways of cities around the world since 2001.
creators.why: One simple object that reacts to each site's geometry is a perfect model for a spatial-mapping AR object.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，2001 年起开展 RedBall Project，把一个直径 4.6 米的红色充气球塞进世界各地城市的小巷、拱门和门洞。
creators.why_zh: 一个简单物体对每个场地的几何形状作出反应，是空间映射 AR 物体的完美范本。

creators.name: Claes Oldenburg and Coosje van Bruggen
creators.bio: Swedish-American Claes Oldenburg (1929–2022) and Dutch-American Coosje van Bruggen (1942–2009) made giant public sculptures of everyday objects such as a spoon, a clothespin and a shuttlecock.
creators.why: Their oversized objects are the original 'giant everyday thing in a park', a move AR creators repeat constantly.
creators.bio_zh: 瑞典裔美国艺术家 Claes Oldenburg（1929–2022）与荷兰裔美国艺术家 Coosje van Bruggen（1942–2009），创作勺子、晾衣夹、羽毛球等日常物品的巨型公共雕塑。
creators.why_zh: 他们的巨型物件是“公园里的巨大日常物品”的原型，AR 创作者一直在重复这一手法。

creators.name: Richard Serra
creators.bio: American sculptor (1938–2024) of massive weathering-steel plates and curves, including East-West/West-East, four 15-metre plates across a Qatari desert.
creators.why: His work is about how a body measures space by walking, the same embodied scale sense AR has to respect.
creators.bio_zh: 美国雕塑家（1938–2024），以巨大的耐候钢板和曲面著称，包括横跨卡塔尔沙漠、四块 15 米高钢板组成的《East-West/West-East》。
creators.why_zh: 他的作品关注身体如何通过行走来丈量空间，这正是 AR 必须尊重的身体尺度感。

creators.name: Isamu Noguchi
creators.bio: Japanese-American artist (1904–1988) who treated whole landscapes as sculpture; his last work, Moerenuma Park in Sapporo, turned a landfill into a park of geometric hills.
creators.why: Moerenuma shows land shaped as a playable sculpture, a direct reference for designing AR in parks.
creators.bio_zh: 日裔美国艺术家（1904–1988），把整片风景当作雕塑；他的最后作品札幌 Moerenuma 公园把垃圾填埋场变成由几何山丘组成的公园。
creators.why_zh: Moerenuma 展示了被塑造成可玩雕塑的土地，是在公园里设计 AR 的直接参考。

creators.name: Fujiko Nakaya
creators.bio: Japanese artist who since 1970 has made fog sculptures: timed clouds of pure water mist that roll over gardens, ponds and buildings and react to wind.
creators.why: Her fog is a real volumetric medium that people walk into and that the weather shapes, a benchmark for volumetric AR effects.
creators.bio_zh: 日本艺术家，自 1970 年起创作雾雕塑：按时间释放的纯水雾在花园、池塘和建筑上翻滚，并随风变化。
creators.why_zh: 她的雾是人可以走进去、由天气塑造的真实体积介质，是体积化 AR 效果的标杆。

creators.name: Amanda Parer
creators.bio: Australian artist whose giant glowing inflatable rabbits (Intrude) sit in parks and squares, a comment on the rabbit plague in Australia.
creators.why: Giant soft animals in a city square are one of the easiest AR scenes to prototype, and her work shows how to add a message to them.
creators.bio_zh: 澳大利亚艺术家，她的巨型发光充气兔子《Intrude》出现在公园和广场上，暗指澳大利亚的兔灾。
creators.why_zh: 城市广场上的巨型柔软动物是最容易做原型的 AR 场景之一，她的作品展示了如何为它们加上信息。

creators.name: Charles Pétillon
creators.bio: French artist whose Invasions series fills houses, courtyards and landscapes with thousands of white balloons, including a 100,000-balloon heart in Covent Garden.
creators.why: His balloon clouds show how a mass of one simple element can re-map a familiar place.
creators.bio_zh: 法国艺术家，《Invasions》系列用成千上万只白色气球填满房屋、庭院和风景，包括伦敦 Covent Garden 中由十万只气球组成的“心脏”。
creators.why_zh: 他的气球云说明，一种简单元素的大量聚集就能重新映射一个熟悉的地方。

creators.name: Ana Mendieta
creators.based: Iowa / New York, US (born Havana, Cuba)
creators.bio: Cuban-American artist (1948–1985) whose Silueta series pressed, burned and planted the outline of her body into earth, sand, mud and water.
creators.why: Her body-shaped traces show how a silhouette left in nature can carry presence after the person has gone.
creators.bio_zh: 古巴裔美国艺术家（1948–1985），《Silueta》系列把她身体的轮廓压入、烧入或种进泥土、沙子、泥浆和水中。
creators.why_zh: 她留在自然中的人形痕迹说明，一个轮廓可以在人离开之后仍然承载“在场”。
creators.based_zh: 艾奥瓦 / 纽约，美国（生于古巴哈瓦那）

creators.name: Lita Albuquerque
creators.bio: American artist who places pigment, stones and spheres in deserts and ice fields to map the stars onto the ground, including Stellar Axis in Antarctica.
creators.why: Stellar Axis literally maps the sky onto the ground, a model for AR that links celestial data to a walkable site.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，在沙漠和冰原上摆放颜料、石头和球体，把星图映射到地面，包括南极的《Stellar Axis》。
creators.why_zh: 《Stellar Axis》真的把天空映射到了地面，是把天文数据与可行走场地相连的 AR 范本。

creators.name: herman de vries
creators.bio: Dutch artist and former biologist who fences off small pieces of land as sanctuaries, letting nature grow undisturbed inside cities.
creators.why: His sanctuaries make an invisible process (wild growth) the whole work, marked only by a boundary.
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰艺术家，曾是生物学家，他把小块土地围起来作为“圣所”，让自然在城市中不受干扰地生长。
creators.why_zh: 他的圣所让一个看不见的过程（野生生长）成为作品的全部，只用一道边界来标记。

creators.name: Hamish Fulton
creators.bio: British artist who defines his art as walking; he records long walks in text and photographs and leads slow group walks in cities.
creators.why: His group walks show that a shared rule for moving through a place can be the whole artwork, useful for location-based AR scores.
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，把行走定义为自己的艺术；用文字和照片记录长途行走，也在城市中带领缓慢的集体行走。
creators.why_zh: 他的集体行走说明，一条共同的移动规则就可以是整件作品，对位置型 AR 的“行动乐谱”很有用。

creators.name: Spencer Byles
creators.bio: British artist who spends a year at a time in a forest, building large sculptures only from what he finds there and leaving them to decay.
creators.why: His hidden forest works are discovered by walking, like geo-anchored AR pieces off the main path.
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，每次在一片森林里待上一年，只用在那里找到的材料建造大型雕塑，然后任其腐朽。
creators.why_zh: 他藏在森林里的作品要靠行走去发现，就像偏离主路的地理锚定 AR 作品。

creators.name: Richard Shilling
creators.bio: British artist who makes ephemeral works from leaves, stones, ice and sticks outdoors, photographs and films them, and teaches land art workshops.
creators.why: His colour-sorted leaves and balanced stones are small, fast pieces that map well to quick AR sketching exercises.
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，在户外用树叶、石头、冰和树枝创作短暂作品，拍照和拍摄记录，并开设大地艺术工作坊。
creators.why_zh: 他按颜色排列的树叶和平衡的石头是小而快的作品，很适合改编成快速 AR 草图练习。

creators.name: Jon Foreman
creators.bio: Welsh artist (Sculpt the World) who arranges beach stones by size and colour into spirals and circles before the tide returns.
creators.why: His sorted stones show how order imposed on natural materials instantly reads as intention, a trick for AR layouts too.
creators.bio_zh: 威尔士艺术家（Sculpt the World），在潮水回来之前，把海滩上的石头按大小和颜色排成螺旋和圆圈。
creators.why_zh: 他排列的石头说明，给自然材料施加秩序会立刻被读成“有意为之”，这也是 AR 布局的技巧。
creators.based_zh: 彭布罗克郡，威尔士，英国

creators.name: Choi Jeong-hwa (최정화)
creators.bio: South Korean artist known for colourful installations of cheap plastic objects and giant inflatable flowers and fruit that breathe in public squares.
creators.why: His breathing lotus shows how one slow, looping motion can make an object feel alive in a plaza.
creators.bio_zh: 韩国艺术家，以廉价塑料物件组成的彩色装置和在公共广场上“呼吸”的巨型充气花果闻名。
creators.why_zh: 他会呼吸的莲花说明，一个缓慢循环的动作就能让广场上的物体显得有生命。

creators.name: Niki de Saint Phalle
creators.bio: French-American artist (1930–2002) who built the Tarot Garden in Tuscany, a hillside of giant mosaic-covered figures based on tarot cards.
creators.why: Her garden is a walkable world of characters placed in a real landscape, the dream of many AR theme parks.
creators.bio_zh: 法裔美国艺术家（1930–2002），在托斯卡纳建造了《Tarot Garden》，一片布满以塔罗牌为原型的巨型马赛克人像的山坡。
creators.why_zh: 她的花园是一个把角色放进真实风景、可以漫步其中的世界，正是许多 AR 主题乐园的梦想。
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 托斯卡纳，意大利

creators.name: Louise Bourgeois
creators.bio: French-American artist (1911–2010) whose giant steel spider Maman, over nine metres tall, stands in plazas in Ottawa, Bilbao, Tokyo and elsewhere.
creators.why: Maman shows how a single giant creature with emotional meaning can dominate and protect a public space.
creators.bio_zh: 法裔美国艺术家（1911–2010），她高逾九米的钢制巨蛛《Maman》矗立在渥太华、毕尔巴鄂、东京等地的广场上。
creators.why_zh: 《Maman》说明一个带有情感意义的巨大生物可以主宰并守护一个公共空间。
creators.based_zh: 纽约，美国（生于法国巴黎）

creators.name: Jeff Koons
creators.bio: American artist known for balloon-animal sculptures and Puppy, a 12-metre West Highland terrier covered in living flowers outside the Guggenheim Bilbao.
creators.why: Puppy is a living, seasonal surface on a giant figure, a reference for AR objects whose materials change over time.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，以气球动物雕塑和《Puppy》闻名，后者是古根海姆毕尔巴鄂美术馆门外一只高 12 米、覆满鲜花的西高地白㹴。
creators.why_zh: 《Puppy》是巨型形象上一层会随季节变化的活表面，是材质随时间变化的 AR 物体的参考。

creators.name: Yinka Shonibare
creators.bio: British-Nigerian artist whose sculptures use Dutch wax-print fabric to question colonial history, including Nelson's Ship in a Bottle on Trafalgar Square's Fourth Plinth.
creators.why: He answers a historic monument with a new object on a plinth, the same gesture as AR counter-monuments.
creators.bio_zh: 英国-尼日利亚艺术家，用荷兰蜡染布料质疑殖民历史，代表作包括伦敦特拉法加广场“第四基座”上的《Nelson's Ship in a Bottle》。
creators.why_zh: 他用基座上的一个新物体回应历史纪念碑，与 AR“反纪念碑”的手法相同。

creators.name: Tadashi Kawamata (川俣正)
creators.bio: Japanese artist who attaches hut-like structures of scrap wood to buildings, trees and bridges, as if a second, informal city were growing on the first.
creators.why: His tree huts cling to real surfaces, the physical analogue of AR content anchored to building facades.
creators.bio_zh: 日本艺术家，用废旧木材在建筑、树木和桥梁上搭建小屋般的结构，仿佛第二座非正式的城市正在第一座城市上生长。
creators.why_zh: 他的树屋依附在真实表面上，是锚定在建筑立面上的 AR 内容的实体类比。
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 东京，日本

creators.name: Marinus Boezem
creators.bio: Dutch conceptual artist whose Green Cathedral in Flevoland (1987–1996) is 178 poplars planted in the exact floor plan of Reims Cathedral.
creators.why: A building drawn with living trees is a perfect example of an invisible architecture overlaid on land.
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰观念艺术家，他在弗莱福兰的《Green Cathedral》（1987–1996）用 178 棵杨树按兰斯大教堂的平面图种植而成。
creators.why_zh: 用活树“画”出的建筑，是在土地上叠加一座看不见的建筑的完美例子。

creators.name: Ackroyd & Harvey (Heather Ackroyd and Dan Harvey)
creators.bio: British duo who project photographic negatives onto growing grass so that chlorophyll prints the image, and cover buildings and ships with living grass.
creators.why: Their grass photographs use light as a slow printer on a living surface, a poetic cousin of projection AR.
creators.bio_zh: 英国二人组，把照片底片投射到正在生长的草上，让叶绿素“印”出图像，也用活草覆盖建筑和船只。
creators.why_zh: 他们的草地照片把光当作在活表面上缓慢打印的工具，是投影 AR 的诗意近亲。

creators.name: Cornelia Konrads
creators.bio: German artist whose site-specific installations make stones, sticks and fences appear to float, fly apart or dissolve in forests and gardens.
creators.why: Her 'frozen explosions' of natural material look like a paused simulation, an easy bridge to AR physics effects.
creators.bio_zh: 德国艺术家，她的场域装置让石头、树枝和栅栏在森林和花园中看起来像在漂浮、飞散或消解。
creators.why_zh: 她用自然材料制造的“凝固爆炸”看起来像暂停的模拟，是通往 AR 物理效果的便捷桥梁。

creators.name: Sam Van Aken
creators.bio: American artist who grafts up to 40 varieties of stone fruit onto one tree, so it blossoms in many colours in spring.
creators.why: The Tree of 40 Fruit is a living, time-based artwork that reveals its design only in one season.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，把多达 40 个品种的核果嫁接到同一棵树上，让它在春天开出多种颜色的花。
creators.why_zh: 《Tree of 40 Fruit》是一件活的、基于时间的作品，只在一个季节里显露其设计。

creators.name: Dennis Hlynsky
creators.bio: American artist and RISD professor who processes ordinary video of birds and insects so each animal leaves a trail, revealing flocking patterns.
creators.why: His frame-accumulation videos are the simplest demo of motion trails on real footage, directly transferable to AR camera effects.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家、罗德岛设计学院教授，处理普通的鸟类和昆虫视频，让每只动物都留下轨迹，揭示群体飞行的图案。
creators.why_zh: 他的帧累积视频是在真实画面上叠加运动轨迹的最简单示范，可以直接迁移到 AR 相机特效。
creators.based_zh: 普罗维登斯，罗得岛，美国

creators.name: Stephen Orlando
creators.bio: Canadian engineer-photographer whose Motion Exposure series attaches colour-changing LED sticks to paddles, swimmers and athletes to draw their motion in long exposures.
creators.why: His colour-coded light trails show time as colour along a path, a precise visual grammar for AR motion trails.
creators.bio_zh: 加拿大工程师兼摄影师，《Motion Exposure》系列把会变色的 LED 灯棒装在船桨、泳者和运动员身上，用长曝光画出他们的运动。
creators.why_zh: 他按时间编码颜色的光迹，把时间表现为路径上的颜色，是 AR 运动轨迹的精确视觉语法。

works.title: Another Place
works.description: One hundred cast-iron figures of the artist's body stand spread over three kilometres of Crosby Beach near Liverpool, all staring out to sea; the tide slowly covers and reveals them.
works.description_zh: 一百尊以艺术家身体翻铸的铸铁人像分布在利物浦附近 Crosby 海滩约三公里的范围内，全部凝望大海；潮水涨落间，它们被慢慢淹没又重新露出。
works.idea_en: Many identical figures facing one horizon turn a whole beach into a stage: the same trick an AR scene can use by spreading copies of one anchor across a site.
works.idea_zh: 许多相同的人像面对同一条地平线，把整片海滩变成舞台：AR 场景也可以把同一个锚点的副本铺满整个场地，得到同样效果。
works.technique: Life-size cast-iron casts of the artist's body are fixed on foundations at different distances from the shore, so the tide and the viewer's distance vary how much of each is visible.
works.technique_zh: 以艺术家身体为模、等身大小的铸铁人像固定在距海岸不同距离的基座上，潮水和观者距离共同决定每尊人像露出多少。
works.exercise_en: Place 20 copies of one scanned human figure across a school field in WebXR or AR Foundation, all facing the same compass direction, and walk among them. Twist: add a rising virtual water plane that hides the figures one by one.
works.exercise_zh: 在 WebXR 或 AR Foundation 中把同一个扫描人像复制 20 份，分散放在学校操场上，全部朝向同一个方位，然后在其间行走；变体：加入一个缓缓上升的虚拟水面，让人像一个个被淹没。

works.title: Event Horizon
works.description: Thirty-one body-form figures are placed on rooftops and pavements across a city (London, New York, São Paulo, Hong Kong), so people suddenly notice a lone man standing on the edge of a building.
works.description_zh: 三十一尊人像被安放在城市（伦敦、纽约、圣保罗、香港）的屋顶和街道上，路人会突然注意到有个孤独的人站在楼顶边缘。
works.idea_en: A figure on a skyline makes people look up and scan the city, showing that one well-placed AR character can redirect a crowd's attention.
works.idea_zh: 天际线上的一个人形让人们抬头扫视整座城市，说明一个放对位置的 AR 角色就能引导人群的注意力。
works.technique: Identical figures are mounted on rooftops at varied distances from a central viewpoint so that the eye links them into a constellation across the skyline.
works.technique_zh: 相同的人像被安装在与中心视点距离不同的屋顶上，让视线把它们在天际线上连成一个星座。
works.exercise_en: Anchor five life-size figures with geospatial AR (ARCore Geospatial API or Niantic Lightship) on rooftops visible from one plaza, and ask classmates to find them all. Twist: make each figure turn to face the nearest viewer.
works.exercise_zh: 用地理空间 AR（ARCore Geospatial API 或 Niantic Lightship）在一个广场可见的五处屋顶上放置等身人像，让同学把它们全部找出来；变体：让每个人像转身面向离它最近的观者。

works.title: Angel of the North
works.description: A 20-metre steel angel with 54-metre wings stands on a former colliery hill beside the A1 motorway at Gateshead, seen by about 90,000 drivers a day.
works.description_zh: 一座高 20 米、翼展 54 米的钢铁天使矗立在盖茨黑德 A1 公路旁一座旧煤矿山丘上，每天约有九万名司机从它身边经过。
works.idea_en: A single giant figure on a hill becomes a landmark people navigate by, a reminder that the scale and silhouette of an AR landmark matter more than detail.
works.idea_zh: 山丘上的一个巨大人形成为人们辨认方向的地标，提醒我们 AR 地标的尺度与轮廓比细节更重要。
works.technique: The body-form is built from ribbed weathering steel sections anchored 20 metres into the hill so it can withstand winds of over 160 km/h.
works.technique_zh: 人形由带肋的耐候钢分段构成，锚入山体 20 米深，足以抵抗时速 160 公里以上的风。
works.exercise_en: Place a 20-metre virtual figure on the tallest point visible from your campus in AR and test from how far away its silhouette is still readable. Twist: let its wings open only when the viewer is moving fast (walking vs. driving speed).
works.exercise_zh: 在 AR 中把一个 20 米高的虚拟人形放在校园可见的最高点上，测试从多远还能认出它的轮廓；变体：只有当观者快速移动（步行与车速）时翅膀才展开。

works.title: Horizon Field
works.description: One hundred cast-iron figures stand across 150 square kilometres of the Vorarlberg Alps, each at exactly 2,039 metres above sea level, so hikers meet them on slopes, ridges and near huts.
works.description_zh: 一百尊铸铁人像分布在奥地利福拉尔贝格州 150 平方公里的阿尔卑斯山区，每一尊都精确位于海拔 2039 米处，登山者会在山坡、山脊和小屋旁与它们相遇。
works.idea_en: All figures sit on one invisible contour line, so the landscape itself draws a horizontal line through the mountains: an AR layer can reveal a hidden datum in the same way.
works.idea_zh: 所有人像都位于同一条看不见的等高线上，于是山体本身在群山间画出一条水平线：AR 图层可以用同样方式揭示隐藏的基准面。
works.technique: Each figure was placed by survey at the same altitude, turning a contour line from the map into a visible, walkable line of bodies.
works.technique_zh: 每尊人像都经测量放置在同一海拔，把地图上的一条等高线变成一条看得见、走得到的人体连线。
works.exercise_en: Use a phone's barometer or GPS altitude in a WebXR page to place a virtual marker whenever the user is at one chosen height on a hill or staircase. Twist: have the whole class walk and leave markers, then view the shared contour line together.
works.exercise_zh: 在 WebXR 页面中读取手机气压计或 GPS 海拔，每当用户到达山坡或楼梯上的某个选定高度时放置一个虚拟标记；变体：全班一起走并留下标记，最后一起查看共享的等高线。

works.title: Exposure
works.description: A 26-metre crouching figure made of an open steel lattice sits on a dyke at Lelystad in Flevoland, on land reclaimed from the sea; from close up it dissolves into a web of beams.
works.description_zh: 一个高 26 米、由开放钢结构组成的蹲坐人形位于弗莱福兰省莱利斯塔德的堤坝上，这片土地是从海中围垦而来；走近看，它会溶解成一张钢梁之网。
works.idea_en: The figure reads as a body from far away and as pure structure up close, a lesson in designing AR objects for two viewing distances.
works.idea_zh: 远看是身体，近看是纯粹结构，这是为两种观看距离设计 AR 物体的一课。
works.technique: A digitised body pose was converted into a network of 14,000 steel members of varying length, so the lattice resolves into a figure only at a distance.
works.technique_zh: 把数字化的身体姿态转换成由 14000 根长短不一的钢构件组成的网络，只有从远处才会聚合成人形。
works.exercise_en: Convert a scanned body into a point-and-line wireframe (Blender geometry nodes) and place it outdoors in AR at 20 metres tall. Twist: fade the lines out as the viewer walks closer so the body disappears when you reach it.
works.exercise_zh: 把扫描人体转换成点线框架（Blender 几何节点），在户外 AR 中放置为 20 米高；变体：观者越走越近时线条逐渐淡出，走到跟前时身体完全消失。

works.title: Inside Australia
works.description: Fifty-one thin black figures, based on body scans of the residents of the tiny town of Menzies, stand scattered over ten square kilometres of the dry salt lake Lake Ballard in Western Australia.
works.description_zh: 五十一尊纤细的黑色人像以西澳小镇 Menzies 居民的身体扫描为原型，散布在干涸盐湖 Lake Ballard 约十平方公里的湖面上。
works.idea_en: Scanning a whole community and placing their slimmed bodies in the desert makes a town's population visible as a landscape, something AR could do with volunteers' scans.
works.idea_zh: 扫描整个社区，把他们被“削瘦”的身体放在沙漠里，让一个小镇的人口变成一片风景；AR 也可以用志愿者的扫描做到这一点。
works.technique: Laser scans of each resident were digitally reduced to a thin core, then cast in an alloy that the salt and sun slowly rust.
works.technique_zh: 每位居民的激光扫描被数字化“削减”到只剩纤细的核心，然后用会被盐和阳光慢慢锈蚀的合金铸成。
works.exercise_en: Scan five classmates with Polycam, scale each model's thickness down to 30% in Blender, and place them far apart on a field in AR. Twist: tag each figure with its owner's spoken sentence that plays when you reach it.
works.exercise_zh: 用 Polycam 扫描五位同学，在 Blender 中把每个模型的厚度缩到 30%，再在 AR 中把它们相隔很远地放在操场上；变体：每个人像附带其本人的一句话，走到跟前时播放。

works.title: Time Horizon
works.description: One hundred iron body casts are placed across a park (first in Calabria, later at Houghton Hall in Norfolk), all at the same height above sea level, so some are buried to the neck and others stand on columns.
works.description_zh: 一百尊铸铁人像分布在一片园林中（先在卡拉布里亚，后在诺福克的 Houghton Hall），全部位于同一海拔，于是有的被埋到脖子，有的站在高柱上。
works.idea_en: Keeping every figure on one absolute height makes the uneven ground visible, a way to use AR objects as measuring devices for terrain.
works.idea_zh: 让每个人像都保持在同一绝对高度，使起伏的地面显形，这是把 AR 物体当作地形测量工具的方法。
works.technique: Figures are set on plinths or sunk into pits so that all their heads share one surveyed altitude regardless of the terrain beneath.
works.technique_zh: 人像或立于基座之上，或沉入坑中，使所有头部都处在同一测量海拔，与下方地形无关。
works.exercise_en: In AR Foundation, place ten figures on a sloping lawn and lock all of their heads to one world-space height, filling the gap below with a column or hiding them in the ground. Twist: let viewers drag the shared height up and down live.
works.exercise_zh: 在 AR Foundation 中把十个人像放在倾斜草坪上，并把它们的头部锁定在同一世界高度，下方空缺用柱子补足或让人像埋入地下；变体：让观者实时上下拖动这个共享高度。

works.title: 6 Times
works.description: Six life-size iron figures stand along the Water of Leith in Edinburgh, from the Gallery of Modern Art to the sea, four of them in the river itself, forming a walk through the city.
works.description_zh: 六尊等身铸铁人像沿爱丁堡的利斯河分布，从现代艺术馆一直到海边，其中四尊直接站在河水中，形成一条穿越城市的步行路线。
works.idea_en: Placing a figure at intervals along a river turns a walk into a narrative sequence, a structure location-based AR tours can copy.
works.idea_zh: 沿河间隔放置人像，把一次步行变成叙事序列，这种结构可以直接用于位置型 AR 导览。
works.technique: Identical figures are fixed on concrete footings in the riverbed and on the banks at irregular intervals along a four-mile route.
works.technique_zh: 相同的人像被固定在河床与河岸的混凝土基础上，沿约六公里的路线不规则分布。
works.exercise_en: Design a six-stop AR walk along a street or stream with 8th Wall or Lens Studio, placing one figure per stop, each a little closer to water. Twist: each figure points toward the next one so the walk needs no map.
works.exercise_zh: 用 8th Wall 或 Lens Studio 沿一条街道或小溪设计六站 AR 步行路线，每站放一个人像，一个比一个更接近水面；变体：每个人像都指向下一个人像，让整条路线无需地图。

works.title: Field for the British Isles
works.description: About 40,000 small clay figures, each shaped by hand by families in St Helens and pressed with two eye holes, fill a room from wall to wall and all look up at the visitor in the doorway.
works.description_zh: 约四万个小陶土人偶由圣海伦斯的家庭手工捏制，每个都戳出两个眼洞，从墙到墙铺满一个房间，全部抬头望向站在门口的观众。
works.idea_en: Tens of thousands of eyes looking back at you reverse who is watching whom, a strong idea for AR crowds that react to gaze.
works.idea_zh: 成千上万双眼睛回望着你，颠倒了“谁在看谁”，这是会对视线作出反应的 AR 人群的有力创意。
works.technique: Community volunteers each formed figures from a fist-sized lump of clay with two pencil-made eyes; the only rule was that they face the viewer.
works.technique_zh: 社区志愿者每人用拳头大小的泥块捏出人偶，用铅笔戳出两只眼睛；唯一的规则是它们必须面向观者。
works.exercise_en: Ask every student to model one tiny creature in a 3D app and combine them into a crowd of hundreds in AR, all rotating to face the phone. Twist: the crowd only looks at you when you stand still.
works.exercise_zh: 让每位学生用 3D 应用做一个小生物，在 AR 中组合成数百个的群体，全部转向手机；变体：只有当你静止不动时，人群才会看向你。

works.title: Another Time (Margate)
works.description: A single iron figure stands on the tidal rocks in front of Turner Contemporary in Margate, submerged at high tide and fully revealed at low tide.
works.description_zh: 一尊铸铁人像站在马盖特 Turner Contemporary 美术馆前的潮间带礁石上，涨潮时被淹没，退潮时完整显露。
works.idea_en: One figure in the sea becomes a clock for the tide, showing how an AR object can visualise a slow natural rhythm by how much of it is visible.
works.idea_zh: 海中的一个人像成了潮汐的时钟，说明 AR 物体可以通过露出多少来呈现缓慢的自然节律。
works.technique: A solid iron cast is bolted to the rock foreshore at a height chosen so that the tide range crosses the whole body.
works.technique_zh: 实心铸铁人像被固定在前滩礁石上，高度经过选择，使潮差恰好覆盖整个身体。
works.exercise_en: Fetch live tide data from a public API and drive a virtual water plane around an AR figure placed on a beach or a campus lawn. Twist: show where the water will be in six hours as a ghost line on the figure.
works.exercise_zh: 从公开 API 获取实时潮汐数据，驱动放在海滩或校园草坪上的 AR 人像周围的虚拟水面；变体：用一条幽灵线在人像上标出六小时后的水位。

works.title: LAND
works.description: For the 50th anniversary of the Landmark Trust, five iron figures in different poses were placed at five historic sites around the UK coast and waterways, such as a Martello tower and a sea-washed bay.
works.description_zh: 为纪念地标信托（Landmark Trust）成立 50 周年，五尊姿态各异的铸铁人像被安放在英国海岸与水道边的五处历史遗址，例如一座马泰洛塔和一处被海浪冲刷的海湾。
works.idea_en: Spreading five figures across a country connects distant sites into one work, a model for multi-location AR campaigns.
works.idea_zh: 把五个人像分散在全国各地，把遥远的场所连成一件作品，这是多地点 AR 活动的范本。
works.technique: Each cast-iron body was posed in response to its site (standing, crouching, looking) and installed for one year at a place where visitors could stay overnight.
works.technique_zh: 每尊铸铁人像的姿态都回应其所在场地（站立、蹲坐、凝望），在游客可以留宿的地方展出一年。
works.exercise_en: Create five AR figures, each tied by geolocation to a different building on campus, with a pose that answers that building. Twist: the fifth figure only appears once a user has visited the other four.
works.exercise_zh: 制作五个 AR 人像，各自用地理位置绑定到校园中的不同建筑，姿态回应该建筑；变体：只有当用户去过另外四处后，第五个人像才会出现。

works.title: Ornithographies
works.description: A short film of the Ornithographies project: flights of gulls, swallows and starlings are shown as solid ribbons and braids that hang in the sky, with a soundtrack made from the birds' own waveforms.
works.description_zh: Ornithographies 项目的短片：海鸥、燕子和椋鸟的飞行被呈现为悬在天空中的实体飘带和发辫，配乐由鸟的声波生成。
works.idea_en: Stacking time into one frame makes the invisible shape of flight visible: the basic recipe for any AR motion trail over real footage.
works.idea_zh: 把时间叠进一帧，让飞行的隐形形状显现：这是在真实画面上做任何 AR 运动轨迹的基本配方。
works.technique: Bou records birds with a high-frame-rate video camera, then merges the frames of each flight into one image by keeping, per pixel, the darkest or most different value against the sky.
works.technique_zh: Bou 用高帧率摄像机拍摄飞鸟，再逐像素保留与天空差异最大（或最暗）的值，把每次飞行的所有帧合成一张图像。
works.exercise_en: Build a phone camera effect (Lens Studio or a WebGL shader) that keeps a fading buffer of the last two seconds of dark pixels against the sky, and point it at birds or passing cars. Twist: colour each trail by time so the start of the flight is blue and the end is red.
works.exercise_zh: 做一个手机相机特效（Lens Studio 或 WebGL 着色器），保留最近两秒内比天空更暗的像素并让其渐隐，对准飞鸟或过往车辆；变体：按时间给轨迹上色，飞行起点为蓝、终点为红。

works.title: Murmurations
works.description: Starling flocks drawing shifting shapes over the sky are traced so the whole murmuration reads as a moving sculpture; when a peregrine falcon attacks, the traces show the flock splitting and reforming.
works.description_zh: 椋鸟群在天空中变换形状，被描绘成一件运动的雕塑；当游隼发动攻击时，轨迹展示鸟群如何分裂又重组。
works.idea_en: Tracing a flock shows that form can emerge from many local decisions without a leader, an idea for AR swarms that react to a predator (the user).
works.idea_zh: 描绘鸟群说明形态可以在没有领导者的情况下从许多局部决策中涌现，这为会对“捕食者”（用户）作出反应的 AR 群体提供了思路。
works.technique: The Ornithographies trail effect is applied to long takes of starling murmurations so each bird leaves a short, fading line.
works.technique_zh: 把 Ornithographies 的轨迹效果应用到椋鸟群的长镜头上，让每只鸟留下一条短暂、渐隐的线。
works.exercise_en: Program a boids flock in Unity or three.js, place it in AR above a courtyard, and draw a short trail behind every bird. Twist: make the phone position a predator the flock avoids.
works.exercise_zh: 在 Unity 或 three.js 中编写 boids 鸟群，放在 AR 中的庭院上空，并在每只鸟身后画出短轨迹；变体：把手机位置当作捕食者，让鸟群躲避它。

works.title: Emergence
works.description: Real footage of starling flocks is inverted and slowed down so each bird's relation to the whole becomes readable, over a soundtrack of nightingale, owl and starling calls slowed ten to twenty times.
works.description_zh: 真实的椋鸟群影像被反相并放慢，使每只鸟与整体的关系变得清晰可读；配乐是放慢十到二十倍的夜莺、猫头鹰和椋鸟叫声。
works.idea_en: Slowing and inverting reality is enough to reveal a hidden system, a cheap and strong AR filter idea.
works.idea_zh: 放慢和反相现实就足以揭示一个隐藏的系统，这是一个成本低、效果强的 AR 滤镜创意。
works.technique: The footage is colour-inverted and time-stretched, and bird calls are pitch-shifted down by slowing them, likely in standard video and audio editors.
works.technique_zh: 影像被色彩反相并拉伸时间，鸟鸣通过放慢而降调，很可能使用常规的视频与音频编辑软件完成。
works.exercise_en: Make a camera filter that inverts colours and plays the live microphone input slowed down four times, then walk through a park with it. Twist: slow the image only where something moves.
works.exercise_zh: 做一个相机滤镜，反相画面并把实时麦克风声音放慢四倍播放，然后带着它穿过公园；变体：只在有东西移动的区域放慢画面。

works.title: Tous les oiseaux du monde
works.description: Made with UCLouvain, the film asks whether we could ever count all the birds in the world: a computer-vision system frames each flying bird with coordinates while a text model answers with fluent nonsense.
works.description_zh: 与鲁汶大学合作完成的影片提出一个问题：我们能数清世界上所有的鸟吗？计算机视觉系统为每只飞鸟框出坐标，而一个文本模型则给出通顺却空洞的回答。
works.idea_en: Showing the machine's bounding boxes on nature exposes what the camera 'sees', a useful critical move for AR object detection.
works.idea_zh: 把机器在自然中画出的检测框显示出来，暴露了相机“看见”的东西，这对 AR 物体识别是一种有用的批判手法。
works.technique: A detector trained on bird silhouettes draws boxes and coordinates over each bird in the footage, alongside text from a pre-ChatGPT language model.
works.technique_zh: 一个用鸟类剪影训练的检测器在画面中的每只鸟上画出方框与坐标，并配以一个早于 ChatGPT 的语言模型生成的文字。
works.exercise_en: Run a COCO object detector (for example TensorFlow.js or Lens Studio ML) on a live camera feed outdoors and display a running count of 'birds' and 'people'. Twist: let the count also invent a poetic caption for each detection.
works.exercise_zh: 在户外实时相机画面上运行 COCO 物体检测器（如 TensorFlow.js 或 Lens Studio ML），显示“鸟”和“人”的累计数量；变体：为每个检测结果同时生成一句诗意的说明。

works.title: One for Sorrow
works.description: Made for the Birdsong Project, the film starts with plain footage of birds, then lets the traces appear and pile up, ending with mirrored swift trails that suggest symbols in the sky, like the omens read by Roman augurs.
works.description_zh: 为 Birdsong Project 创作的影片从普通的飞鸟画面开始，随后轨迹逐渐出现并叠加，最后以镜像的雨燕轨迹结尾，仿佛天空中浮现出符号，就像古罗马占卜师解读的征兆。
works.idea_en: Mirroring natural traces makes people read meaning into them, a way for AR to turn random motion into a message.
works.idea_zh: 镜像处理自然轨迹会让人从中读出意义，这是 AR 把随机运动变成信息的一种方式。
works.technique: The trail effect is revealed gradually over the footage and then mirrored left-right to create symmetric, sign-like shapes.
works.technique_zh: 轨迹效果在画面中逐步显现，随后左右镜像，形成对称、像符号一样的形状。
works.exercise_en: Add a vertical mirror to a live motion-trail camera effect so anything moving in front of the phone draws a symmetric figure. Twist: save the most symmetric figure of the day as a 'sign' and pin it in AR where it was made.
works.exercise_zh: 给实时运动轨迹相机特效加一面竖直镜像，让手机前任何移动的物体都画出对称图形；变体：把当天最对称的图形保存为“征兆”，钉在其产生的位置上供 AR 查看。

works.title: Entomographies
works.description: With entomologist Adrian Smith, Bou turns the flight of insects into glowing patterns, drawing attention to their beauty and to their decline.
works.description_zh: Bou 与昆虫学家 Adrian Smith 合作，把昆虫的飞行变成发光的图案，让人注意到它们的美，也注意到它们正在减少。
works.idea_en: The same trace method works at insect scale, so an AR trail effect can make the tiny motion around a flower visible.
works.idea_zh: 同样的轨迹方法也适用于昆虫尺度，因此 AR 轨迹效果可以让花朵周围细微的运动显形。
works.technique: High-speed macro footage of insects in flight is stacked frame by frame into single trails, likely against dark or controlled backgrounds.
works.technique_zh: 昆虫飞行的高速微距影像被逐帧叠合成轨迹，很可能是在黑色或受控背景下拍摄。
works.exercise_en: Point a phone with a trail-shader effect at a flowering bush for five minutes and record the pattern of bees and flies. Twist: switch the trail colour according to the flight speed so hovering and darting look different.
works.exercise_zh: 用带轨迹着色器特效的手机对准一丛开花的灌木拍摄五分钟，记录蜜蜂和苍蝇的飞行图案；变体：按飞行速度切换轨迹颜色，让悬停与疾飞看起来不同。

works.title: Fluctus
works.description: Life-size, top-down images capture the instant a bird takes off after being released from a wildlife recovery centre, showing wings, colour and structure from a bird's-eye view.
works.description_zh: 等大的俯视图像捕捉了鸟从野生动物救护中心放飞、振翅起飞的那一瞬间，以鸟瞰视角展示翅膀、颜色和结构。
works.idea_en: Changing the viewpoint (from below the sky to above the bird) reveals a new structure, a reminder that AR can offer impossible camera angles on real things.
works.idea_zh: 改变视点（从仰望天空到俯视飞鸟）揭示出新的结构，提醒我们 AR 可以为真实事物提供不可能的机位。
works.technique: A camera mounted above the release point shoots the bird's first wing strokes; sequential frames are likely composited to show the take-off motion.
works.technique_zh: 安装在放飞点上方的相机拍下鸟最初的几次振翅，很可能把连续帧合成以呈现起飞的动作。
works.exercise_en: Place a scanned or rigged bird in AR and let the user switch between a ground view and a locked top-down view of its take-off. Twist: leave a translucent copy of the bird at every wingbeat so the take-off becomes a sculpture.
works.exercise_zh: 在 AR 中放一只扫描或绑定骨骼的鸟，让用户在地面视角和锁定的俯视视角之间切换观看它起飞；变体：每次振翅都留下一个半透明副本，让起飞过程变成一件雕塑。

works.title: Rivers and Tides
works.description: Thomas Riedelsheimer's film follows Goldsworthy building icicle spirals, leaf chains that float down a river and a stone cone that the incoming tide swallows.
works.description_zh: Thomas Riedelsheimer 的纪录片跟拍 Goldsworthy 用冰柱搭出螺旋、让树叶链顺流漂走，以及建造一个被涨潮吞没的石锥。
works.idea_en: The artwork includes its own disappearance: designing for how a piece decays or is taken by nature is as important as how it appears.
works.idea_zh: 作品包含了它自身的消失：设计作品如何衰败或被自然带走，与设计它如何出现同样重要。
works.technique: He uses only found materials and their own properties (freezing, floating, balancing), working with the time of day and the tide.
works.technique_zh: 他只使用现场找到的材料及其自身特性（冻结、漂浮、平衡），配合一天中的时间和潮汐工作。
works.exercise_en: Build an AR sculpture from scanned leaves or stones on a real riverbank or puddle and program it to fall apart when a timer or the user's approach triggers it. Twist: let the pieces drift along the real water direction the user traces.
works.exercise_zh: 在真实的河岸或水洼边，用扫描的树叶或石头搭一个 AR 雕塑，并编程让它在计时器或用户靠近时解体；变体：让碎片沿用户描出的真实水流方向漂走。

works.title: Leaning into the Wind
works.description: The second film by Thomas Riedelsheimer shows Goldsworthy using his own body: walking through a hedge, lying on the ground as rain starts so a dry 'rain shadow' remains, and throwing leaves.
works.description_zh: Thomas Riedelsheimer 的第二部影片展示 Goldsworthy 用身体创作：穿过一道树篱，在雨开始落下时躺在地上留下干燥的“雨影”，以及抛撒树叶。
works.idea_en: A body-shaped dry patch on wet ground is a trace of presence that disappears in minutes, a direct idea for AR silhouettes left by users.
works.idea_zh: 湿地上人形的干燥痕迹是几分钟内便会消失的“在场”痕迹，直接启发了由用户留下的 AR 剪影。
works.technique: The rain shadows are made by lying still on dry ground at the start of a shower and standing up once the ground around is wet.
works.technique_zh: “雨影”的做法是在阵雨开始时静躺在干燥地面上，等周围地面湿透后再站起来。
works.exercise_en: Use body segmentation (Lens Studio or MediaPipe) to capture a user's silhouette and leave it as a fading shadow decal on the ground in AR. Twist: shadows fade faster when many people walk over the same spot.
works.exercise_zh: 用人体分割（Lens Studio 或 MediaPipe）捕捉用户剪影，在 AR 中把它作为逐渐淡去的影子贴花留在地面上；变体：多人踩过同一位置时影子消退得更快。

works.title: Storm King Wall
works.description: A dry-stone wall snakes between trees in a forest at Storm King Art Center, then runs down a hill, disappears into a pond and re-emerges on the far side.
works.description_zh: 一道干垒石墙在 Storm King 艺术中心的林中蛇行穿过树木，随后下坡，没入池塘，又在对岸重新出现。
works.idea_en: A line that dodges trees and dives under water shows how an anchored path can react to the site rather than ignore it.
works.idea_zh: 一条会绕开树木、潜入水下的线，说明锚定的路径可以回应场地，而不是无视它。
works.technique: Wallers built the 690-metre wall by hand from stones of old field walls on the site, curving it around each tree.
works.technique_zh: 工匠们用场地上旧田埂墙的石头手工垒起这道长 690 米的墙，并让它绕着每一棵树弯曲。
works.exercise_en: Generate an AR line with Unity AR Foundation plane and mesh detection that winds around detected obstacles (people, chairs, trees) instead of crossing them. Twist: let the line dive under a detected floor plane and re-emerge.
works.exercise_zh: 用 Unity AR Foundation 的平面与网格检测生成一条 AR 线，让它绕开检测到的障碍物（人、椅子、树）而不是穿过去；变体：让线潜入检测到的地面之下再重新冒出。

works.title: Spire
works.description: Thirty-seven cypress trunks from the Presidio's old forest are bound into a 30-metre spire, which the newly planted trees around it will slowly grow up to hide.
works.description_zh: 37 根来自 Presidio 老林的柏树树干被捆扎成一座 30 米高的尖塔，周围新种的树木会慢慢长高并把它遮住。
works.idea_en: The work is designed to be absorbed by the forest over decades, a model for AR installations with a planned lifespan.
works.idea_zh: 作品被设计为在几十年中被森林吸收，是具有计划寿命的 AR 装置的范本。
works.technique: Felled trunks are stacked and fixed into a tall cone at the centre of a replanting area so that surrounding growth measures time.
works.technique_zh: 伐下的树干在重新造林区中心被堆叠固定成高锥，让周围的生长成为时间的度量。
works.exercise_en: Anchor a tall AR spire in a park and add simulated trees that grow a little every day the app is opened, until they hide it. Twist: let every visitor plant one virtual tree that joins the forest for everyone.
works.exercise_zh: 在公园里锚定一座高大的 AR 尖塔，并加入每天打开应用时都会长高一点的模拟树木，直到它们把尖塔遮住；变体：让每位访客种下一棵所有人都能看到的虚拟树。

works.title: Wood Line
works.description: A 350-metre line of eucalyptus logs, laid end to end, snakes along the floor of a Presidio forest between the trunks, inviting people to walk on and beside it.
works.description_zh: 一条由桉树原木首尾相接而成、长约 350 米的线在 Presidio 森林的地面上蛇行穿过树干之间，邀请人们在上面和旁边行走。
works.idea_en: A single line on the ground turns a forest into a path and a drawing at once, the simplest form of guidance AR can give.
works.idea_zh: 地面上的一条线同时把森林变成了路径和绘画，这是 AR 能提供的最简单的引导形式。
works.technique: Branches from trees felled for forest management are laid in a continuous curving line, partly sunk into the ground.
works.technique_zh: 因森林管理而伐下的树枝被铺成一条连续弯曲的线，部分埋入地面。
works.exercise_en: Draw a continuous AR line on the ground with Lens Studio or WebXR hit-testing as you walk through trees, save it, and let the next visitor follow it. Twist: the line slowly sinks into the ground over a week.
works.exercise_zh: 边走过树林边用 Lens Studio 或 WebXR 命中测试在地面上画出一条连续的 AR 线，保存后让下一位访客沿线行走；变体：一周内这条线慢慢沉入地下。

works.title: Tree Fall
works.description: Inside a former gunpowder store in the Presidio, a eucalyptus trunk is suspended from the vaulted ceiling, and both ceiling and trunk are covered in cracked clay.
works.description_zh: 在 Presidio 一座旧火药库内，一根桉树树干悬挂在拱顶下，天花板和树干都覆盖着干裂的泥土。
works.idea_en: Bringing a tree indoors and coating the room around it creates a portal-like space, the same effect AR world replacement aims for.
works.idea_zh: 把一棵树带进室内并给整个房间覆上泥层，营造出传送门般的空间，这正是 AR 替换世界想要达到的效果。
works.technique: The trunk is hung from the ceiling and the surfaces are plastered with local clay that dries and cracks into a pattern.
works.technique_zh: 树干悬挂于天花板，墙面和树干抹上当地的泥土，干燥后裂出纹理。
works.exercise_en: Use LiDAR scene reconstruction (ARKit) to cover a real room's ceiling and walls with a cracked-clay material and hang a virtual tree from the ceiling. Twist: the cracks spread wherever the user looks longest.
works.exercise_zh: 用激光雷达场景重建（ARKit）给真实房间的天花板和墙面覆上干裂泥土材质，并从天花板上悬挂一棵虚拟树；变体：用户注视最久的地方裂纹蔓延得最快。

works.title: Earth Wall
works.description: A wall of rammed earth built from the Presidio's soil encloses the branches of a eucalyptus tree, which reach out through the wall's surface.
works.description_zh: 一面用 Presidio 泥土夯筑的墙把一棵桉树的枝干包在其中，枝条从墙面伸出。
works.idea_en: An object half-inside a wall reads as something passing through a boundary, a classic AR occlusion effect in physical form.
works.idea_zh: 一个半截嵌在墙里的物体看起来像正在穿过边界，这是实体版的经典 AR 遮挡效果。
works.technique: Earth from the site is compacted in layers inside formwork around the branches so they appear to grow out of the finished wall.
works.technique_zh: 现场的泥土在围绕枝干的模板中分层夯实，拆模后枝干仿佛从墙中长出。
works.exercise_en: Use AR occlusion (ARKit people and scene occlusion) to make a virtual branch or creature appear to push out of a real wall. Twist: let it pull back in when touched.
works.exercise_zh: 用 AR 遮挡（ARKit 人物与场景遮挡）让一根虚拟树枝或一只生物看起来正从真实墙面中钻出；变体：被触碰时它会缩回墙内。

works.title: Refuges d'Art
works.description: In the mountains of Haute-Provence, Goldsworthy restored ruined farms, chapels and sheepfolds along a 150-kilometre hiking route and placed works inside; some can be slept in.
works.description_zh: 在上普罗旺斯的山区，Goldsworthy 沿一条 150 公里的徒步路线修复了废弃的农舍、小教堂和羊圈，并在其中放置作品，有些还可以留宿。
works.idea_en: Art that you reach only by walking days through a landscape makes the journey part of the work, a model for long-distance AR trails.
works.idea_zh: 只有步行几天穿越风景才能抵达的艺术，让旅程成为作品的一部分，是长距离 AR 路线的范本。
works.technique: Old stone buildings are rebuilt as shelters and each contains a stone or clay work made for that site, linked by a waymarked trail.
works.technique_zh: 旧石屋被重建为避难所，每处都有一件为该地制作的石或泥作品，并由一条有路标的步道相连。
works.exercise_en: Design a multi-day or multi-hour AR hiking route with geolocated 'refuges' where a virtual work appears only if the user arrived on foot (checked by step count). Twist: each refuge shows traces left by earlier hikers.
works.exercise_zh: 设计一条持续数小时或数天的 AR 徒步路线，在地理定位的“避难所”处，只有步行抵达的用户（以步数判断）才能看到虚拟作品；变体：每个避难所都显示先前徒步者留下的痕迹。

works.title: Wrapped Coast
works.description: At Little Bay in Sydney, about 2.5 kilometres of rocky coastline and cliffs were wrapped in 92,900 square metres of fabric tied with rope for ten weeks.
works.description_zh: 在悉尼的 Little Bay，约 2.5 公里长的岩石海岸和悬崖被 92900 平方米的织物包裹，并用绳索捆扎，持续十周。
works.idea_en: Wrapping hides detail and reveals form: a single material laid over a landscape is the physical version of an AR mesh shader.
works.idea_zh: 包裹隐藏细节、凸显形体：一种材料覆盖整片风景，是 AR 网格着色器的实体版本。
works.technique: Synthetic fabric was draped over the cliffs and held with 56 kilometres of rope by volunteers and climbers.
works.technique_zh: 志愿者和攀岩者把合成织物铺在悬崖上，用总长 56 公里的绳子固定。
works.exercise_en: Use LiDAR mesh reconstruction to cover a real rock, bench or car with a draped fabric material in AR, with rope lines following the surface. Twist: let the wind (random noise) ripple the fabric.
works.exercise_zh: 用激光雷达网格重建在 AR 中给真实的石头、长椅或汽车盖上一层垂坠织物材质，并让绳线沿表面走；变体：让“风”（随机噪声）吹动织物起伏。

works.title: Valley Curtain
works.description: An orange nylon curtain 400 metres wide was hung across Rifle Gap in the Colorado Rockies; it stood for only 28 hours before a gale forced its removal.
works.description_zh: 一道宽 400 米的橙色尼龙帘幕悬挂在科罗拉多落基山脉的 Rifle Gap 峡谷之间，仅仅 28 小时后便因大风被迫拆除。
works.idea_en: A thin coloured plane across a valley shows how one flat element can re-scale a whole landscape, and how weather is part of the design.
works.idea_zh: 横跨山谷的一片薄薄的彩色平面说明，一个平面元素就能重塑整片风景的尺度，而天气也是设计的一部分。
works.technique: The curtain hung from steel cables anchored in the mountainsides, with openings to let the wind pass (the Maysles brothers documented its making).
works.technique_zh: 帘幕悬挂在锚固于两侧山体的钢缆上，并留有开口让风通过（Maysles 兄弟记录了其制作过程）。
works.exercise_en: Span a huge orange AR plane between two real landmarks (buildings or trees) using geospatial anchors and watch it from far away. Twist: tie its survival to live wind-speed data so it tears when the wind is strong.
works.exercise_zh: 用地理空间锚点在两个真实地标（建筑或树木）之间拉起一面巨大的橙色 AR 平面，从远处观看；变体：把它的存续绑定到实时风速数据，风大时帘幕会撕裂。

works.title: Running Fence
works.description: A white fabric fence 5.5 metres high ran for 39.4 kilometres across the hills of Sonoma and Marin counties in California and into the Pacific Ocean, for two weeks.
works.description_zh: 一道高 5.5 米的白色织物围栏穿过加州索诺玛县和马林县的丘陵，延伸 39.4 公里后没入太平洋，持续两周。
works.idea_en: A line that follows the land for 40 kilometres makes the topography readable, a strong idea for AR lines drawn on terrain data.
works.idea_zh: 沿地形延伸 40 公里的一条线让地貌变得可读，这是在地形数据上绘制 AR 线的有力创意。
works.technique: 2,050 fabric panels hung from steel cables between poles followed the ground's curves, installed with the ranchers' permission.
works.technique_zh: 2050 块织物挂在立柱之间的钢缆上，随地面起伏延伸，在牧场主的许可下安装。
works.exercise_en: Use a digital elevation model and a geospatial AR SDK to draw a white fence line along a real ridge that you can see from a viewpoint. Twist: extend the line into the sea or a lake and let it sink.
works.exercise_zh: 使用数字高程模型和地理空间 AR SDK，沿一条从某个观景点可见的真实山脊画出白色围栏线；变体：让线一直延伸进海或湖中并沉没。

works.title: Surrounded Islands
works.description: Eleven islands in Miami's Biscayne Bay were each surrounded by a floating skirt of pink fabric extending 61 metres into the water, for two weeks.
works.description_zh: 迈阿密比斯坎湾的十一座小岛各自被一圈粉红色浮布环绕，布面向水中延伸 61 米，持续两周。
works.idea_en: Outlining existing things with a bright halo makes them visible as a set, a basic AR highlighting technique at landscape scale.
works.idea_zh: 用明亮的光环勾勒已有之物，让它们作为一个整体被看见，这是风景尺度上的基本 AR 高亮技巧。
works.technique: Sewn pink panels were attached to floating booms anchored around each island's shoreline and unfurled on the same day.
works.technique_zh: 缝制好的粉色布面固定在环绕各岛岸线的浮栏上，并在同一天展开。
works.exercise_en: Detect objects on a table or in a courtyard with segmentation and draw a pink offset outline around each on the ground plane in AR. Twist: the outlines grow when two objects are close, merging into one shape.
works.exercise_zh: 用分割检测桌面或庭院中的物体，在 AR 地面上为每个物体画出粉色外扩轮廓；变体：两个物体靠近时轮廓变大并合并成一个形状。

works.title: The Umbrellas, Japan–USA
works.description: 1,340 blue umbrellas opened in a valley in Ibaraki, Japan, and 1,760 yellow umbrellas in the hills north of Los Angeles at the same time, each six metres tall.
works.description_zh: 1340 把蓝色大伞在日本茨城县的山谷中、1760 把黄色大伞在洛杉矶以北的丘陵中同时撑开，每把高六米。
works.idea_en: Two simultaneous sites in two countries, one colour each, show how a shared event can link distant places, a model for synchronous multi-site AR.
works.idea_zh: 两个国家的两处场地同时展开，各用一种颜色，展示了共享事件如何连接遥远的地方，是同步多地点 AR 的范本。
works.technique: Steel-framed umbrellas were set in bases across private and public land and opened on the same morning in both countries.
works.technique_zh: 钢骨大伞安放在私人和公共土地上的底座中，并在两国的同一个早晨同时撑开。
works.exercise_en: Build a shared AR session (Niantic Lightship or Photon) where students in two classrooms each place coloured umbrellas and see the other room's umbrellas appear as a mirrored layer. Twist: umbrellas only open when both sites are online.
works.exercise_zh: 搭建一个共享 AR 会话（Niantic Lightship 或 Photon），让两个教室的学生各自放置彩色伞，并以镜像图层看到对方房间的伞出现；变体：只有两个地点都在线时伞才会撑开。

works.title: Wrapped Reichstag
works.description: After 24 years of lobbying, the German parliament building in Berlin was wrapped in silver fabric and blue rope for two weeks, drawing about five million visitors.
works.description_zh: 经过 24 年的游说，柏林的德国国会大厦被银色织物和蓝色绳索包裹两周，吸引了约五百万名观众。
works.idea_en: Hiding a loaded symbol makes people look at it again; an AR 'wrap' filter on a monument can do the same.
works.idea_zh: 把一个意义沉重的象征隐藏起来，反而让人们重新审视它；在纪念建筑上做 AR“包裹”滤镜也能达到同样效果。
works.technique: About 100,000 square metres of fabric and 15.6 kilometres of rope were fitted over steel frames that protected the building's sculptures.
works.technique_zh: 约十万平方米的织物和 15.6 公里的绳索覆盖在保护建筑雕塑的钢框架上。
works.exercise_en: Use Lens Studio City Landmarker or a scanned building model to wrap a famous local building in silver cloth in AR. Twist: let people pull the rope to unwrap it together.
works.exercise_zh: 用 Lens Studio 的城市地标模板或扫描的建筑模型，在 AR 中给当地一座著名建筑包上银色布料；变体：让大家一起拉动绳索把它解开。

works.title: The Gates, Central Park
works.description: 7,503 saffron-coloured gates with hanging fabric lined 37 kilometres of footpaths in New York's Central Park for 16 days in February.
works.description_zh: 7503 座挂着织物的藏红花色门廊沿纽约中央公园 37 公里长的步道排列，在二月展出 16 天。
works.idea_en: Repeating one element along every path turns a park's circulation into a visible drawing, a strong pattern for AR wayfinding.
works.idea_zh: 沿每条小径重复同一个元素，把公园的动线变成一幅可见的图，这是 AR 导航的有力模式。
works.technique: Gates of different widths were made to fit each path and stood on steel bases, so no holes were drilled in the park.
works.technique_zh: 门廊按每条小径的宽度定制，立在钢制底座上，因此没有在公园里打一个孔。
works.exercise_en: Generate a repeated saffron gate every five metres along a path traced from GPS or a map in an AR walk. Twist: gates only unfurl in front of the walker and fold up behind them.
works.exercise_zh: 在一次 AR 步行中，沿着根据 GPS 或地图描出的路径每五米生成一座藏红花色门；变体：门只在行人前方展开，在身后收起。

works.title: The Gates in augmented reality (Bloomberg Connects)
works.description: For the 20th anniversary of The Gates, an AR experience in the Bloomberg Connects app puts the saffron gates back along Central Park's paths on visitors' phones.
works.description_zh: 在《The Gates》20 周年之际，Bloomberg Connects 应用中的 AR 体验让藏红花色门廊重新出现在观众手机中的中央公园小径上。
works.idea_en: A vanished temporary artwork can return in AR at its original site, turning an archive into a walkable experience.
works.idea_zh: 一件已消失的临时作品可以在原址以 AR 形式回归，把档案变成可以走进的体验。
works.technique: Likely geospatial AR anchoring of 3D gate models to their documented positions along the park paths.
works.technique_zh: 很可能是把 3D 门廊模型按照有记录的位置，以地理空间 AR 锚定在公园小径上。
works.exercise_en: Choose a past event or vanished structure on your campus, find an archive photo, and re-place it in AR at its exact original spot. Twist: add a 'then/now' slider that crossfades the old scene with the live view.
works.exercise_zh: 选择校园里一件过去的事件或已消失的建筑，找到档案照片，并在 AR 中把它放回原来的确切位置；变体：加入“过去/现在”滑块，在旧场景与实时画面之间淡入淡出。

works.title: The Floating Piers
works.description: Three kilometres of walkways covered in yellow fabric floated on Lake Iseo in Italy, letting 1.2 million people walk on water between the shore and two islands for 16 days.
works.description_zh: 三公里长、覆盖黄色织物的浮动步道漂在意大利伊塞奥湖上，16 天内让 120 万人在岸边与两座岛之间“行走于水面”。
works.idea_en: Walking on water is felt through the body (the piers move under your feet), a reminder that AR can borrow real physical sensations.
works.idea_zh: 水上行走是通过身体感受到的（浮桥在脚下起伏），提醒我们 AR 可以借用真实的身体感受。
works.technique: 220,000 floating polyethylene cubes formed a modular dock covered with shimmering fabric that changed colour when wet.
works.technique_zh: 22 万个漂浮的聚乙烯方块组成模块化浮台，上面覆盖着遇水变色的闪光织物。
works.exercise_en: In AR, lay a glowing path across a real pond or a car park and add subtle camera sway when the user walks on it. Twist: the path only extends one step ahead of the walker.
works.exercise_zh: 在 AR 中，在真实的池塘或停车场上铺一条发光小路，当用户走上去时给镜头加入轻微晃动；变体：小路只在行人前方延伸一步。

works.title: The London Mastaba
works.description: A 20-metre-high trapezoidal stack of 7,506 painted oil barrels floated on the Serpentine lake in Hyde Park for three months, its colours reflected in the water.
works.description_zh: 由 7506 个彩绘油桶堆成、高 20 米的梯形体漂浮在海德公园蛇形湖上三个月，色彩倒映在水中。
works.idea_en: A single abstract volume on water, doubled by its reflection, shows how simple geometry plus reflection can feel monumental in AR.
works.idea_zh: 水面上的一个抽象体块被倒影加倍，说明简单几何加上反射就能在 AR 中产生纪念碑感。
works.technique: Barrels were fixed onto a scaffold on a floating platform anchored with 32 anchors to the lakebed.
works.technique_zh: 油桶固定在一个浮动平台的脚手架上，平台用 32 个锚固定在湖底。
works.exercise_en: Place a large AR block on a real water surface with a planar reflection shader (Unity URP) so it doubles in the water. Twist: build it from hundreds of small instanced barrels that visitors can recolour.
works.exercise_zh: 在真实水面上放置一个大型 AR 体块，并用平面反射着色器（Unity URP）让它在水中成双；变体：用数百个实例化的小油桶拼成它，访客可以给它们重新上色。

works.title: L'Arc de Triomphe, Wrapped
works.description: Realised after Christo's death, the Arc de Triomphe in Paris was wrapped in 25,000 square metres of silver-blue fabric and 3,000 metres of red rope for 16 days.
works.description_zh: 在 Christo 去世后实现：巴黎凯旋门被 25000 平方米的银蓝色织物和 3000 米红色绳索包裹 16 天。
works.idea_en: A familiar monument turned into a soft, shimmering object is exactly what a city-scale AR material swap feels like.
works.idea_zh: 一座熟悉的纪念碑变成柔软闪亮的物体，这正是城市尺度 AR 材质替换带来的感觉。
works.technique: Recyclable fabric was lowered from the top over steel frames that protected the reliefs, and tied with red polypropylene rope.
works.technique_zh: 可回收织物从顶部沿保护浮雕的钢框架放下，再用红色聚丙烯绳捆扎。
works.exercise_en: Take a photogrammetry model of a local monument and, in AR, swap its material for silver fabric with red rope lines. Twist: the fabric shimmers more when the wind (device motion) is stronger.
works.exercise_zh: 取一座当地纪念碑的摄影测量模型，在 AR 中把它的材质替换为带红色绳线的银色织物；变体：“风”（设备晃动）越大，织物越闪亮。

works.title: Spiral Jetty
works.description: A 457-metre coil of black basalt and earth spirals counter-clockwise into the red-tinted water of Utah's Great Salt Lake; it was submerged for decades and is now crusted white with salt.
works.description_zh: 一条长 457 米、由黑色玄武岩和泥土构成的螺旋逆时针伸入犹他州大盐湖泛红的湖水中；它曾被淹没数十年，如今覆满白色盐壳。
works.idea_en: A shape that you can walk along but only fully see from the air shows how AR content can reward both the ground view and the overview.
works.idea_zh: 一个可以沿着行走、却只有从空中才能看全的形状，说明 AR 内容可以同时奖励地面视角和鸟瞰视角。
works.technique: Dump trucks and a front loader pushed 6,650 tons of rock and earth into the shallow lake along a staked spiral path.
works.technique_zh: 自卸卡车和装载机沿着打桩标出的螺旋路径，把 6650 吨岩石和泥土推入浅湖中。
works.exercise_en: Walk a spiral on a field while a WebXR app records your GPS trace, then view the path as a raised AR ribbon from above using a 'drone view' toggle. Twist: raise and lower a virtual water level that hides and reveals the spiral.
works.exercise_zh: 在操场上走出一个螺旋，同时用 WebXR 应用记录 GPS 轨迹，然后用“无人机视角”开关从上方查看隆起的 AR 飘带；变体：升降一个虚拟水位，让螺旋时隐时现。

works.title: Broken Circle/Spiral Hill
works.description: In a sand quarry in Emmen, Netherlands, a half-land, half-water circle faces a small hill with a white-sand path spiralling to its top; a huge glacial boulder sits at the circle's centre.
works.description_zh: 在荷兰埃门的一处采砂场中，一个半是陆地半是水面的圆与一座小山相对，白沙小径螺旋盘上山顶；圆心处卧着一块巨大的冰川漂砾。
works.idea_en: Pairing a flat figure (the circle) with a climbable one (the hill) gives two viewpoints on the same work, a classic AR composition pattern.
works.idea_zh: 把一个平面图形（圆）与一个可攀登的图形（山）配对，为同一件作品提供两种视角，这是经典的 AR 构图模式。
works.technique: The circle was dug and built up in the quarry's water and sand, and the hill's path was shaped with white sand and topsoil.
works.technique_zh: 圆是在采砂场的水和沙中挖出并堆筑而成，山上的小径则用白沙和表土塑形。
works.exercise_en: Place a flat AR ring on the ground and a small AR hill beside it that users can 'climb' by walking up real stairs to look down on the ring. Twist: the ring only closes into a full circle when seen from the top.
works.exercise_zh: 在地面上放一个扁平的 AR 圆环，旁边放一座小 AR 山，用户走上真实的楼梯即可“登山”俯视圆环；变体：只有从顶端看时圆环才会闭合成完整的圆。

works.title: Amarillo Ramp
works.description: A curved earth ramp rising from the ground and ending mid-air sits in a dry lake on a Texas ranch; Smithson died in a plane crash while surveying it, and Nancy Holt and friends completed it.
works.description_zh: 一条从地面升起、戛然止于半空的弧形土坡位于得克萨斯州一处牧场的干湖中；Smithson 在勘测时因飞机失事遇难，由 Nancy Holt 与朋友们完成。
works.idea_en: A ramp that curls up and stops invites the body to walk into the sky, a strong lead-in shape for AR content that continues where the ground ends.
works.idea_zh: 一条卷起后戛然而止的坡道引导身体走向天空，是在地面终止处接续 AR 内容的有力引导形状。
works.technique: Earth and red shale were piled into a rising, curving ramp that forms an open circle about 46 metres across.
works.technique_zh: 泥土和红色页岩被堆成一条上升的弧形坡道，构成一个直径约 46 米的开口圆。
works.exercise_en: Stand at the end of a real ramp or staircase and extend it with an AR ramp that continues into the air. Twist: the virtual ramp grows only while someone is walking on the real one.
works.exercise_zh: 站在真实坡道或楼梯的尽头，用一条延伸到空中的 AR 坡道把它接续下去；变体：只有有人在真实坡道上行走时，虚拟坡道才会生长。

works.title: Partially Buried Woodshed
works.description: At Kent State University, Smithson had a backhoe pile earth onto a woodshed until its central beam cracked, then left it to decay; only traces remain today.
works.description_zh: 在肯特州立大学，Smithson 让挖掘机把泥土堆在一座木棚上，直到其中央横梁断裂，然后任其腐朽；如今只剩痕迹。
works.idea_en: An artwork that is meant to decay turns entropy into content, a useful stance for AR works that degrade on purpose.
works.idea_zh: 一件注定要衰败的作品把熵变成了内容，这对有意自我退化的 AR 作品是很有用的立场。
works.technique: Twenty truckloads of earth were dumped on the roof of an existing shed until it broke, fixing a moment of collapse.
works.technique_zh: 二十卡车泥土被倒在一座现成木棚的屋顶上，直到它断裂，定格了坍塌的瞬间。
works.exercise_en: Anchor a small AR building at a spot on campus and program it to lose one element every day the site is visited. Twist: publish a timeline slider so visitors can scrub back to how it looked on day one.
works.exercise_zh: 在校园某处锚定一座小型 AR 建筑，并编程让它在每次有人到访时失去一个构件；变体：发布时间轴滑块，让访客回看它第一天的样子。

works.title: Sun Tunnels
works.description: Four concrete tunnels, each 5.5 metres long, lie in an open X in the Great Basin Desert of Utah, aligned with sunrise and sunset on the solstices; holes in their walls form four constellations of light inside.
works.description_zh: 四条长 5.5 米的混凝土隧道在犹他州大盆地沙漠中呈开放的 X 形排列，对准至日的日出与日落；隧道壁上的孔洞在内部投下四个星座的光点。
works.idea_en: The tunnels frame the sky at precise moments and places, the same logic as an AR experience that only resolves at one time and position.
works.idea_zh: 隧道在精确的时刻与位置框住天空，与只在某个时间和位置成立的 AR 体验逻辑相同。
works.technique: Tunnels were cast with holes sized and placed to match the stars of Draco, Perseus, Columba and Capricorn, and oriented by solar calculation.
works.technique_zh: 隧道浇筑时按天龙座、英仙座、天鸽座和摩羯座的星位开孔并确定孔径，朝向则依据太阳轨迹计算。
works.exercise_en: Compute today's sunset azimuth for your location and place an AR tube on a field that frames the sun exactly at sunset. Twist: punch holes in the tube that match the constellation overhead tonight.
works.exercise_zh: 计算你所在地今天日落的方位角，在操场上放一个 AR 圆筒，让它恰好在日落时框住太阳；变体：在圆筒上开孔，孔位对应今晚头顶的星座。

works.title: Dark Star Park
works.description: In Rosslyn, Virginia, large dark spheres, pools and poles are placed so that every 1 August at 9:32 a.m. their shadows line up exactly with outlines drawn on the ground, marking the date the land was bought in 1860.
works.description_zh: 在弗吉尼亚州罗斯林，巨大的深色球体、水池和立杆经过精确摆放，使每年 8 月 1 日上午 9:32 它们的影子与地面上画出的轮廓完全重合，以纪念这片土地在 1860 年被购买的日子。
works.idea_en: A shadow that fits its outline once a year is a clock, an idea AR can replicate by matching virtual shadows to the real sun.
works.idea_zh: 一年只与轮廓吻合一次的影子就是一座钟，AR 可以通过让虚拟阴影匹配真实太阳来复现这一想法。
works.technique: Positions of spheres, poles and ground outlines were calculated from the sun's altitude and azimuth at the anniversary time.
works.technique_zh: 球体、立杆和地面轮廓的位置根据纪念时刻太阳的高度角和方位角计算得出。
works.exercise_en: Place AR spheres on a plaza and draw outlines on the ground where their shadows will fall at a chosen date and time, using a solar-position library. Twist: let each visitor set their own anniversary.
works.exercise_zh: 在广场上放置 AR 球体，并用太阳位置库在地面画出它们在指定日期和时刻的影子轮廓；变体：让每位访客设定自己的纪念日。

works.title: Up and Under
works.description: In a former sand quarry in Nokia, Finland, a long grass-covered earth mound is pierced by concrete tunnels that frame views of the sky, water and each other.
works.description_zh: 在芬兰诺基亚市的一处旧采砂场中，一道长长的覆草土堤被数条混凝土隧道穿过，隧道框住天空、水面以及彼此的景象。
works.idea_en: Tunnels through a mound are viewfinders that tell you exactly where to stand and look, like AR markers that reward one viewpoint.
works.idea_zh: 穿过土堤的隧道就是取景器，明确告诉你站在哪里、看向哪里，就像只奖励某一视点的 AR 标记。
works.technique: Concrete pipes were laid through a shaped earthwork and grassed over; their axes are aligned with the landscape and cardinal points.
works.technique_zh: 混凝土管道穿过塑形后的土方工程并覆盖草皮，轴线与地景和方位对齐。
works.exercise_en: Place three AR tubes through a real hedge or building gap so each frames a different target (a tree, a window, the sky). Twist: show a hidden message only when the user stands inside a tube's axis.
works.exercise_zh: 穿过真实的树篱或建筑空隙放置三根 AR 管道，让每根框住不同的目标（一棵树、一扇窗、天空）；变体：只有当用户站在管道轴线上时才显示隐藏信息。

works.title: Solar Rotary
works.description: At the University of South Florida, a ring with a circular hole on tall poles casts a spot of light that, on specific dates, falls on plaques marking events in local history; on the summer solstice it lands on a central seat.
works.description_zh: 在南佛罗里达大学，高杆上一个带圆孔的环投下一个光斑，在特定日期落在记录当地历史事件的铭牌上；夏至正午时它会落在中央的座椅上。
works.idea_en: Using the sun as a pointer that visits dated plaques turns a plaza into a calendar, a direct model for time-based AR annotations.
works.idea_zh: 把太阳当作指针，按日期依次照亮铭牌，把广场变成日历，这是基于时间的 AR 标注的直接范本。
works.technique: The aperture's position was calculated so the sun spot's path hits each plaque on its anniversary date.
works.technique_zh: 开孔位置经过计算，使光斑的轨迹在每个纪念日恰好照到对应铭牌。
works.exercise_en: Compute where the midday sun spot from a real opening (a window, a gate) falls through the year and pin AR notes on those floor points with the dates of campus events. Twist: the notes light up only when the real sun spot touches them.
works.exercise_zh: 计算一年中正午阳光穿过真实开口（窗户、门洞）后光斑落在地面的位置，在这些点上钉上标注校园事件日期的 AR 便签；变体：只有真实光斑触及时便签才会亮起。

works.title: The Lightning Field
works.description: Four hundred stainless-steel poles stand in a grid one mile by one kilometre in the high desert of New Mexico, their tips forming a perfectly level plane; visitors stay overnight to watch the light change (and occasionally lightning).
works.description_zh: 四百根不锈钢杆在新墨西哥高原沙漠中排成一英里乘一公里的网格，杆尖构成一个绝对水平的面；参观者需在此过夜，观看光线变化（偶尔还有闪电）。
works.idea_en: A strict grid laid over wild land makes both light and terrain readable; AR grids can do the same for invisible fields.
works.idea_zh: 在荒野上铺设严格的网格，让光线和地形都变得可读；AR 网格也可以对看不见的场做同样的事。
works.technique: Poles of varying height (average about 6 metres) were surveyed so their pointed tips align to one horizontal plane over uneven ground.
works.technique_zh: 立杆高度不一（平均约 6 米），经测量使尖端在起伏地面上对齐同一水平面。
works.exercise_en: Lay out a 10×10 grid of thin AR poles on an uneven field with tips locked to one world height, and watch it at sunset. Twist: make poles glow brighter where live weather data reports higher humidity or wind.
works.exercise_zh: 在起伏的场地上布置 10×10 的细 AR 杆网格，杆尖锁定在同一世界高度，并在日落时观看；变体：根据实时天气数据，让湿度或风速更高处的杆发出更亮的光。

works.title: The New York Earth Room
works.description: A SoHo loft in New York is filled with 127 cubic metres of dark soil, 56 centimetres deep; a caretaker waters and rakes it, and visitors look in from the doorway.
works.description_zh: 纽约 SoHo 区的一间阁楼里铺满 127 立方米、深 56 厘米的黑土；有专人浇水、耙平，访客只能从门口向内观看。
works.idea_en: Filling a whole room with one natural material replaces the interior with a landscape, the physical version of AR room replacement.
works.idea_zh: 用一种自然材料填满整个房间，把室内替换成一片风景，是 AR 房间替换的实体版本。
works.technique: Soil is spread evenly across the floor to a fixed depth behind a glass barrier and maintained weekly.
works.technique_zh: 泥土在玻璃挡板后均匀铺满地面至固定深度，每周维护。
